# ngrok documentation: Reference

> Every page in the Reference section of the ngrok docs (265 pages). Each link points to the page's Markdown version.

## Platform API

- [ngrok API Overview](https://ngrok.com/docs/api/index.md): Learn about the ngrok REST API for programmatic access to all ngrok resources including endpoints, domains, and configurations.
- [API Filtering](https://ngrok.com/docs/api/api-filtering.md): Pass CEL expressions in the filter parameter to narrow ngrok API list results, and check which fields you can filter on for each resource.

## Platform API / Gateway / Endpoints

- [Endpoints: List (GET /endpoints)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/list.md): List all agent endpoint configurations in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [Endpoints: Create (POST /endpoints)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/create.md): Create a new agent endpoint configuration for connecting local applications to the ngrok service.
- [Endpoints: Get (GET /endpoints/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific agent endpoint configuration including its status and settings.
- [Endpoints: Delete (DELETE /endpoints/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/delete.md): Delete a specific agent endpoint configuration by its unique identifier.
- [Endpoints: Update (PATCH /endpoints/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/endpoints/update.md): Update an existing agent endpoint configuration with new settings, labels, or metadata.

## Platform API / Gateway / Reserved Addrs

- [Reserved Addrs: List (GET /reserved_addrs)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reservedaddrs/list.md): List all reserved static IP addresses in your ngrok account with optional filtering.
- [Reserved Addrs: Create (POST /reserved_addrs)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reservedaddrs/create.md): Reserve a static IP address for use with your ngrok endpoints and edges.
- [Reserved Addrs: Get (GET /reserved_addrs/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reservedaddrs/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific reserved static IP address including its status and usage.
- [Reserved Addrs: Delete (DELETE /reserved_addrs/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reservedaddrs/delete.md): Release a reserved static IP address by its unique identifier.
- [Reserved Addrs: Update (PATCH /reserved_addrs/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reservedaddrs/update.md): Update an existing reserved static IP address configuration or metadata.

## Platform API / Gateway / Reserved Domains

- [Reserved Domains: List (GET /reserved_domains)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/list.md): List all reserved custom domains in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [Reserved Domains: Create (POST /reserved_domains)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/create.md): Reserve a custom domain for use with your ngrok endpoints and edges.
- [Reserved Domains: Get (GET /reserved_domains/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific reserved domain including its certificate and DNS configuration.
- [Reserved Domains: Delete (DELETE /reserved_domains/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/delete.md): Release a reserved custom domain by its unique identifier.
- [Reserved Domains: Update (PATCH /reserved_domains/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/update.md): Update an existing reserved domain configuration including certificate management settings.
- [Reserved Domains: Deletecertificate (DELETE /reserved_domains/{id}/certificate)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/deletecertificate.md): Delete the TLS certificate associated with a specific reserved domain.
- [Reserved Domains: Deletecertificatemanagementpolicy (DELETE /reserved_domains/{id}/certificate_management_policy)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/reserveddomains/deletecertificatemanagementpolicy.md): Remove the certificate management policy from a specific reserved domain.

## Platform API / Gateway / TLS Certificates

- [TLS Certificates: List (GET /tls_certificates)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tlscertificates/list.md): List all TLS certificates in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [TLS Certificates: Create (POST /tls_certificates)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tlscertificates/create.md): Upload a new TLS certificate for use with your ngrok edges and reserved domains.
- [TLS Certificates: Get (GET /tls_certificates/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tlscertificates/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific TLS certificate including its domains and expiration date.
- [TLS Certificates: Delete (DELETE /tls_certificates/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tlscertificates/delete.md): Delete a specific TLS certificate by its unique identifier.
- [TLS Certificates: Update (PATCH /tls_certificates/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tlscertificates/update.md): Update an existing TLS certificate with new certificate data or private key.

## Platform API / Gateway

- [Kubernetes Operators](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/kubernetes-operators.md): API reference documentation for Kubernetes Operator endpoints used by the ngrok Kubernetes Operator to manage operator state.

## Platform API / Traffic Policy / Certificate Authorities

- [Certificate Authorities: List (GET /certificate_authorities)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/certificateauthorities/list.md): List all certificate authority configurations in your ngrok account with optional filtering.
- [Certificate Authorities: Create (POST /certificate_authorities)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/certificateauthorities/create.md): Create a new certificate authority configuration for custom TLS certificate management in ngrok.
- [Certificate Authorities: Get (GET /certificate_authorities/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/certificateauthorities/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific certificate authority configuration including its certificates.
- [Certificate Authorities: Delete (DELETE /certificate_authorities/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/certificateauthorities/delete.md): Delete a specific certificate authority configuration by its unique identifier.
- [Certificate Authorities: Update (PATCH /certificate_authorities/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/certificateauthorities/update.md): Update an existing certificate authority configuration with new settings or certificates.

## Platform API / Traffic Policy / IP Policies

- [IP Policies: List (GET /ip_policies)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicies/list.md): List all IP policies in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [IP Policies: Create (POST /ip_policies)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicies/create.md): Create a new IP policy for controlling access based on IP address allowlists or denylists.
- [IP Policies: Get (GET /ip_policies/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicies/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific IP policy including its rules and associated resources.
- [IP Policies: Delete (DELETE /ip_policies/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicies/delete.md): Delete a specific IP policy by its unique identifier.
- [IP Policies: Update (PATCH /ip_policies/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicies/update.md): Update an existing IP policy with new rules, description, or metadata.

## Platform API / Traffic Policy / IP Policy Rules

- [IP Policy Rules: List (GET /ip_policy_rules)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicyrules/list.md): List all IP policy rules in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [IP Policy Rules: Create (POST /ip_policy_rules)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicyrules/create.md): Create a new IP policy rule to add an IP address or CIDR block to an IP policy.
- [IP Policy Rules: Get (GET /ip_policy_rules/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicyrules/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific IP policy rule including its IP address or CIDR block.
- [IP Policy Rules: Delete (DELETE /ip_policy_rules/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicyrules/delete.md): Delete a specific IP policy rule by its unique identifier.
- [IP Policy Rules: Update (PATCH /ip_policy_rules/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/ippolicyrules/update.md): Update an existing IP policy rule with a new IP address or CIDR block.

## Platform API / Traffic Policy / Applications / Application Users

- [Application Users: List (GET /app/users)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/applicationusers/list.md): List all application users in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination support.
- [Application Users: Get (GET /app/users/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/applicationusers/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific application user including their roles and permissions.
- [Application Users: Delete (DELETE /app/users/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/applicationusers/delete.md): Delete a specific application user by its unique identifier, removing all associated access.

## Platform API / Traffic Policy / Applications / Application Sessions

- [Application Sessions: List (GET /app/sessions)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/applicationsessions/list.md): List all application sessions in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [Application Sessions: Get (GET /app/sessions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/applicationsessions/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific application session including its status and metadata.
- [Application Sessions: Delete (DELETE /app/sessions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/applicationsessions/delete.md): Delete a specific application session by its unique identifier, terminating the session immediately.

## Platform API / Secure Tunnels / Agent Ingresses

- [Agent Ingresses: Create (POST /agent_ingresses)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/agentingresses/create.md): Create a new agent ingress configuration to define how agents connect to the ngrok service.
- [Agent Ingresses: Get (GET /agent_ingresses/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/agentingresses/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific agent ingress configuration by its unique identifier.
- [Agent Ingresses: Delete (DELETE /agent_ingresses/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/agentingresses/delete.md): Delete a specific agent ingress configuration by its unique identifier.
- [Agent Ingresses: Update (PATCH /agent_ingresses/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/agentingresses/update.md): Update an existing agent ingress configuration with new settings or parameters.

## Platform API / Secure Tunnels / Tunnel Sessions

- [Tunnel Sessions: List (GET /tunnel_sessions)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tunnelsessions/list.md): List all tunnel sessions in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [Tunnel Sessions: Get (GET /tunnel_sessions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tunnelsessions/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific tunnel session including its status and connection information.
- [Tunnel Sessions: Restart (POST /tunnel_sessions/{id}/restart)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tunnelsessions/restart.md): Restart a specific tunnel session, re-establishing the connection to the ngrok service.
- [Tunnel Sessions: Stop (POST /tunnel_sessions/{id}/stop)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tunnelsessions/stop.md): Stop a specific tunnel session, terminating the connection to the ngrok service.
- [Tunnel Sessions: Update (POST /tunnel_sessions/{id}/update)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/tunnelsessions/update.md): Update a specific tunnel session with new configuration or metadata.

## Platform API / Observability / Event Destinations

- [Event Destinations: List (GET /event_destinations)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventdestinations/list.md): List all event destination configurations in your ngrok account with optional filtering.
- [Event Destinations: Create (POST /event_destinations)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventdestinations/create.md): Create a new event destination configuration for receiving ngrok platform events and notifications.

## Platform API / Observability / Event Sources

- [Event Sources: List (GET /event_subscriptions/{subscription_id}/sources)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsources/list.md): List all event sources configured for a specific event subscription.
- [Event Sources: Create (POST /event_subscriptions/{subscription_id}/sources)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsources/create.md): Add a new event source to an existing event subscription for receiving specific event types.
- [Event Sources: Get (GET /event_subscriptions/{subscription_id}/sources/{type})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsources/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific event source within an event subscription.
- [Event Sources: Delete (DELETE /event_subscriptions/{subscription_id}/sources/{type})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsources/delete.md): Remove a specific event source from an event subscription by its type.
- [Event Sources: Update (PATCH /event_subscriptions/{subscription_id}/sources/{type})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsources/update.md): Update an existing event source configuration within an event subscription.

## Platform API / Observability / Event Subscriptions

- [Event Subscriptions: Create (POST /event_subscriptions)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsubscriptions/create.md): Create a new event subscription for receiving and processing ngrok platform events.
- [Event Subscriptions: Get (GET /event_subscriptions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsubscriptions/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific event subscription including its sources and destinations.
- [Event Subscriptions: Delete (DELETE /event_subscriptions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsubscriptions/delete.md): Delete a specific event subscription by its unique identifier.
- [Event Subscriptions: Update (PATCH /event_subscriptions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/eventsubscriptions/update.md): Update an existing event subscription with new sources, destinations, or configuration.

- [IP Restrictions: Update (PATCH /ip_restrictions/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/iprestrictions/update.md): Update an existing IP restriction configuration with new allowed IP addresses or ranges.

## Platform API / IAM / API Keys

- [API Keys: List (GET /api_keys)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/apikeys/list.md): List all API keys in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination support.
- [API Keys: Create (POST /api_keys)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/apikeys/create.md): Create a new API key for authenticating requests to the ngrok API with specific permissions and scopes.
- [API Keys: Get (GET /api_keys/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/apikeys/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific API key including its permissions and metadata.
- [API Keys: Delete (DELETE /api_keys/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/apikeys/delete.md): Delete a specific API key by its unique identifier, immediately revoking its access.
- [API Keys: Update (PATCH /api_keys/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/apikeys/update.md): Update an existing API key's permissions, description, or other metadata.

## Platform API / IAM / SSH Credentials

- [SSH Credentials: Create (POST /ssh_credentials)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/sshcredentials/create.md): Create a new SSH credential for authenticating connections to SSH backends.

- [SSH Credentials: Update (PATCH /ssh_credentials/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/sshcredentials/update.md): Update an existing SSH credential with new private key or metadata.

## Platform API / IAM / Credentials

- [Credentials: List (GET /credentials)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/credentials/list.md): List all credentials in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination support.
- [Credentials: Create (POST /credentials)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/credentials/create.md): Create a new credential for authenticating connections to credential-backed backends.
- [Credentials: Get (GET /credentials/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/credentials/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific credential including its type and associated backends.
- [Credentials: Delete (DELETE /credentials/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/credentials/delete.md): Delete a specific credential by its unique identifier, revoking its access immediately.
- [Credentials: Update (PATCH /credentials/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/credentials/update.md): Update an existing credential's configuration, authentication details, or metadata.

## Platform API / Vaults & Secrets / Secrets

- [Secrets: List (GET /vault_secrets)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/secrets/list.md): List all vault secrets in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination support.
- [Secrets: Create (POST /vault_secrets)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/secrets/create.md): Create a new vault secret for securely storing sensitive values used in ngrok configurations.
- [Secrets: Get (GET /vault_secrets/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/secrets/get.md): Retrieve metadata about a specific vault secret. The secret value itself is never returned.
- [Secrets: Delete (DELETE /vault_secrets/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/secrets/delete.md): Delete a specific vault secret by its unique identifier, permanently removing the stored value.
- [Secrets: Update (PATCH /vault_secrets/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/secrets/update.md): Update an existing vault secret with a new value or modify its metadata.

## Platform API / Vaults & Secrets / Vaults

- [Vaults: List (GET /vaults)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/vaults/list.md): List all vaults in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination support.
- [Vaults: Create (POST /vaults)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/vaults/create.md): Create a new vault for securely storing and managing secrets used in ngrok configurations.
- [Vaults: Get (GET /vaults/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/vaults/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific vault including its metadata and associated secrets count.
- [Vaults: Delete (DELETE /vaults/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/vaults/delete.md): Delete a specific vault by its unique identifier, removing all associated secrets.
- [Vaults: Update (PATCH /vaults/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/vaults/update.md): Update an existing vault with new metadata, description, or configuration settings.
- [Vaults: List secrets (GET /vaults/{id}/secrets)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/vaults/list-secrets.md): List the secrets stored in a specific vault, identified by its unique ID, so you can review what the vault contains.

## Platform API / Deprecated / Bot Users

- [Bot Users: List (GET /bot_users)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/botusers/list.md): List all bot users in your ngrok account. Note: Bot Users are deprecated in favor of Service Users.
- [Bot Users: Create (POST /bot_users)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/botusers/create.md): Create a new bot user for programmatic API access. Note: Bot Users are deprecated in favor of Service Users.
- [Bot Users: Get (GET /bot_users/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/botusers/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific bot user. Note: Bot Users are deprecated in favor of Service Users.
- [Bot Users: Delete (DELETE /bot_users/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/botusers/delete.md): Delete a specific bot user by its unique identifier. Note: Bot Users are deprecated in favor of Service Users.
- [Bot Users: Update (PATCH /bot_users/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/botusers/update.md): Update an existing bot user's configuration. Note: Bot Users are deprecated in favor of Service Users.

## Platform API / Deprecated / Backends / Failover Backends

- [Failover Backends: List (GET /backends/failover)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/failoverbackends/list.md): List all failover backend configurations in your ngrok account with optional filtering and pagination.
- [Failover Backends: Create (POST /backends/failover)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/failoverbackends/create.md): Create a new failover backend for automatically switching between primary and secondary backends based on health.
- [Failover Backends: Get (GET /backends/failover/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/failoverbackends/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific failover backend including its primary and secondary backends.
- [Failover Backends: Delete (DELETE /backends/failover/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/failoverbackends/delete.md): Delete a specific failover backend configuration by its unique identifier.
- [Failover Backends: Update (PATCH /backends/failover/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/failoverbackends/update.md): Update an existing failover backend with new primary or secondary backend configurations.

## Platform API / Deprecated / Backends / HTTP Response Backends

- [HTTP Response Backends: List (GET /backends/http_response)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/httpresponsebackends/list.md): List all HTTP response backend configurations in your ngrok account with optional filtering.
- [HTTP Response Backends: Create (POST /backends/http_response)](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/httpresponsebackends/create.md): Create a new HTTP response backend for returning custom HTTP responses without forwarding requests.
- [HTTP Response Backends: Get (GET /backends/http_response/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/httpresponsebackends/get.md): Retrieve details about a specific HTTP response backend including its response configuration.
- [HTTP Response Backends: Delete (DELETE /backends/http_response/{id})](https://ngrok.com/docs/api-reference/httpresponsebackends/delete.md): Delete a specific HTTP response backend configuration by its unique identifier.

- [Go SDK Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/go.md): Learn how to get started with the ngrok Go SDK to create secure tunnels from your Go applications to the internet.
- [Python SDK Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/python.md): Learn how to get started with the ngrok Python SDK to create secure tunnels from your Python applications to the internet.
- [Rust SDK Quickstart](https://ngrok.com/docs/getting-started/rust.md): Learn how to get started with the ngrok Rust SDK to create secure tunnels from your Rust applications to the internet.

## SDKs / Framework Libraries

- [Framework Libraries](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent-sdks/frameworks/index.md): Put a Next.js, Gin, FastAPI, or Axum app online with one call using ngrok's framework libraries, built on the ngrok SDKs.
- [Next.js Library](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent-sdks/frameworks/nextjs.md): Run next dev with a public ngrok URL using the @ngrok/nextjs command, and configure the endpoint with a Traffic Policy or a reserved domain.
- [Gin Library](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent-sdks/frameworks/gin.md): Put a Gin app online with the ngrok-gin Go library, then give it a reserved domain, a Traffic Policy, or more than one endpoint.
- [FastAPI Library](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent-sdks/frameworks/fastapi.md): Put a FastAPI app online with the ngrok-fastapi Python package, then add a Traffic Policy or open more than one endpoint.
- [Axum Library](https://ngrok.com/docs/agent-sdks/frameworks/axum.md): Put an Axum app online with the ngrok-axum Rust crate, then give it a reserved domain, a Traffic Policy, or more than one endpoint.

## Errors

- [Errors](https://ngrok.com/docs/errors/index.md): How ngrok error codes work, how to use them when troubleshooting or handling errors programmatically, and the most common errors.
- [Errors Reference](https://ngrok.com/docs/errors/reference.md): Complete reference for all ngrok error codes. Find explanations, causes, and fixes for every ngrok tunnel, agent, and API error in one place.
